name: Design Review
description: Five-dimension design audit (frontend UI/UX · server data-model & flow · endpoint spec · daemon-runtime/SDK & local-cache-first · built-in skill/agent-role) executed by a NON-implementing agent. Every dimension must be answered; N/A is allowed only with a stated reason. A dimension the proposal silently skipped must be surfaced as a gap; a proposal that legitimately covers a dimension must not be over-reported.

sampleTasks.title: Five-dimension audit of a proposal that silently skips the daemon/SDK dimension
sampleTasks.prompt:
Run the design-review skill (five-dimension audit) as a NON-implementing reviewer on the PROPOSAL below. Audit it across ALL FIVE dimensions and, for each, give a one-line verdict (covered / gap / N/A-with-reason) BACKED BY THE REAL REPO: `rg` for the actual file this dimension would touch and cite it as `path:line`. --- PROPOSAL: 'Add a per-user daily LLM spend cap. (1) DB: ADD COLUMN `daily_cap_credits` to `im_users` via a new migration; write path updates it in the settings save handler. (2) Endpoint: new `PATCH /api/im/me/spend-cap` (JWT auth) sets the cap; `GET /api/im/me/spend-cap` reads it. (3) Frontend: a new number field in the Settings > Billing page, with an inline error toast when the value is negative.' --- Note what this proposal does NOT address: the daemon/SDK layer runs LLM calls locally and caches spend locally (local-cache-first), so a cloud-only cap that the daemon never learns about will not be enforced on the daemon's LLM path — yet the proposal says nothing about daemon↔cloud sync, offline fallback, or the local spend cache. It also says nothing about the built-in-skill / agent-role dimension. Your audit MUST: (a) walk all five dimensions by name; (b) mark the daemon-runtime/SDK dimension as a GAP (the enforcement hole) rather than silently passing it; (c) either flag the built-in-skill/agent-role dimension as a gap or mark it N/A WITH a stated reason (do not leave it unanswered); (d) not fabricate blocking problems in the three dimensions the proposal legitimately covers (frontend, data-model, endpoint) — note them as covered, listing only genuine residual questions.

--- YOUR REPORT MUST USE THIS MACHINE-CHECKED OUTPUT CONTRACT. The checker looks for each dimension's OWN KEYED LINE and re-reads every citation off disk, so the word appearing elsewhere in your prose does not count as answering that dimension, and an invented path:line is caught.

Five lines, each with its exact key, opening with the verdict, then the reason, then the evidence:
```
- [1] frontend-uiux: covered — <what the proposal covers + residual question> | <path:line>
- [2] server-data-model: covered — <...> | <path:line>
- [3] endpoint-spec: covered — <...> | <path:line>
- [4] daemon-runtime-sdk: gap — <what the hole is and how it actually breaks> | <path:line in the daemon/runtime source that would have to change>
- [5] skill-agent-role: gap — <...> | <path:line>    (or)    N/A — <reason ≥20 chars>
```
Rules the checker enforces: a dimension line must OPEN with `covered`, `gap` or `N/A`; a `covered` or `gap` line must carry at least one `path:line` that resolves on disk (real file, line in range, non-blank) — `rg -n` it, do not guess line numbers; an `N/A` line must carry a reason of at least 20 non-space characters. Dimension [4] must carry the verdict `gap` — rubber-stamping it `covered`, or leaving it off its keyed line while saying 'gap' somewhere else in the prose, FAILS. Citations MUST be repo-root-relative (`src/im/api/routes.ts:314`, never an abbreviated `im/api/routes.ts:314` and never an absolute path); a `rg -c` HIT COUNT is not a line number, write counts as `count=N`.

Then your prose summary: the per-dimension verdict table, the load-bearing finding (the silently-skipped daemon/SDK dimension), and `openQuestions[]`.
expectedArtifacts: five keyed dimension lines (frontend-uiux / server-data-model / endpoint-spec / daemon-runtime-sdk / skill-agent-role), each opening with a verdict and backed by a path:line that resolves on disk or an explicit N/A + reason
the daemon-runtime/SDK dimension carrying the `gap` verdict on its own keyed line (local-cache-first enforcement hole), not silently passed
the built-in-skill/agent-role dimension answered (gap or N/A-with-reason), not left blank
prose summary: verdict table, load-bearing finding, openQuestions — the three covered dimensions not over-reported as fabricated blockers

acceptanceCriteria.label: all five dimensions answered on their own keyed line — each backed by a citation re-verified on disk, or an explicit N/A with a real reason (no dimension may be silently dropped)

the silently-skipped daemon-runtime/SDK dimension carries the `gap` verdict ON ITS OWN keyed line with on-disk evidence — a `covered` rubber stamp, or the word 'gap' floating elsewhere in the prose, fails
